statement: Let vals(x) be the sequence of i64 values of the nodes of x from front to back, and let m = floor(n/2). The function returns a result r and vals(r) = vals(head)[0..m] ++ vals(head)[m+1..n]; equivalently, r is exactly the list obtained from head by deleting the 0-based node at index m. In particular, if n = 1 then r is Nil.
preconditions: Let n be the number of nodes in head. Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and every node value lies in [1, 100000].

statement: The function returns a result r for some List r; it does not fail.
preconditions: Let n be the number of nodes in head. Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and every node value lies in [1, 100000].

statement: Let vals(x) be the sequence of values of the nodes of x from front to back. The function returns a result r and len(vals(r)) = n - 1.
preconditions: Let n be the number of nodes in head. Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and every node value lies in [1, 100000].

statement: Let vals(x) be the sequence of values of the nodes of x from front to back. The function returns a result r and, for every i with 0 <= i < m, vals(r)[i] = vals(head)[i].
preconditions: Let n be the number of nodes in head, and let m = floor(n/2). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and every node value lies in [1, 100000].

statement: Let vals(x) be the sequence of values of the nodes of x from front to back. The function returns a result r and, for every j with m <= j < n - 1, vals(r)[j] = vals(head)[j + 1].
preconditions: Let n be the number of nodes in head, and let m = floor(n/2). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and every node value lies in [1, 100000].

statement: Let vals(x) be the sequence of values of the nodes of x from front to back. The function returns a result r and len(vals(r)) >= 1 and vals(r)[0] = vals(head)[0].
preconditions: Let n be the number of nodes in head. Assume 1 <= n <= 100000, every node value lies in [1, 100000], and n >= 2.

statement: Let vals(x) be the sequence of values of the nodes of x from front to back. The function returns a result r and len(vals(r)) >= 1 and vals(r)[n - 2] = vals(head)[n - 1].
preconditions: Let n be the number of nodes in head. Assume 1 <= n <= 100000, every node value lies in [1, 100000], and n >= 3.

statement: Let vals(x) be the sequence of values of the nodes of x from front to back, and let count(xs, v) be the number of occurrences of value v in the sequence xs. The function returns a result r and, for every i64 value v, count(vals(r), v) = count(vals(head), v) - (if v = vals(head)[m] then 1 else 0).
preconditions: Let n be the number of nodes in head, and let m = floor(n/2). Assume 1 <= n <= 100000 and every node value lies in [1, 100000].
